s: Which one of the following correctly describes the position of the Right to Property under the Constitution as it stood in 1950?
o: It was guaranteed only under Article 31 as a legal right
It was a DPSP under Article 39
It was a statutory right under the Representation of the People Act, 1951
It was a Fundamental Right under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31
x: In 1950, the Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Article 19(1)(f), relating to acquiring, holding and disposing of property, and Article 31, relating to deprivation and acquisition of property.
tq: Use the historical position of the right rather than its present constitutional status.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: The 1st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951 inserted which of the following provisions to protect land reform laws?
o: Articles 39A and 43B and the Eleventh Schedule
Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule
Articles 32A and 33 and the Eighth Schedule
Articles 30(1A) and 300A and the Tenth Schedule
x: The 1st Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and created the Ninth Schedule to provide protection to land reform laws.
tq: Match the amendment with the constitutional provisions introduced by it.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional amendments affecting the Right to Property:
1. The 4th Amendment was enacted in 1955.
2. The 17th Amendment was enacted in 1964.
3. The 25th Amendment was enacted in 1971.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: All three statements are correct: the 4th, 17th and 25th Amendments were enacted in 1955, 1964 and 1971 respectively, and each affected the constitutional treatment of property and compensation.
tq: Check each year independently before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: With reference to the 17th Amendment relating to property, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: It inserted Article 300A in Part XII
It made all land acquisition free from judicial review
It provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on payment of market value
It abolished Article 31 altogether
x: The 17th Amendment provided that land under personal cultivation could be acquired only on payment of market value.
tq: Identify the amendment-specific detail instead of choosing the broader property-right changes.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 brought about which one of the following changes?
o: It shifted Article 21A from Part IV to Part III
It inserted Articles 31A and 31B in Part III
It converted the Right to Property into a Fundamental Right available only to citizens
It deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from Part III and placed the Right to Property under Article 300A
x: The 44th Amendment deleted Article 19(1)(f) and Article 31 from Part III and made property a constitutional legal right under Article 300A in Part XII, Chapter IV.
tq: Distinguish the deleting amendment from the earlier amendments that protected land reforms.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: Article 300A provides that—
o: No citizen shall be deprived of property except by executive order
No company shall be deprived of property under any circumstances
No person shall be deprived of property except with the consent of Parliament
No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law
x: Article 300A states that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.
tq: Recall the exact constitutional wording and avoid replacing 'authority of law' with executive action.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: Which one of the following correctly explains the present constitutional status of the Right to Property?
o: It is a constitutional legal right under Article 300A, available to all persons
It is a constitutional legal right enforceable against legislation under Article 32
It is only a statutory right available to citizens under the RPA, 1951
It is a Fundamental Right enforceable under Article 32
x: The Right to Property is a constitutional legal right under Article 300A. It is available to all persons, including citizens, non-citizens and companies, but is not a Fundamental Right enforceable under Article 32.
tq: Separate Fundamental Rights from constitutional legal rights by status, beneficiaries and remedy.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: A person is dispossessed of property by an executive order without any authority of law. Which constitutional provision is most directly attracted?
o: Article 300A
Article 31 as a continuing Fundamental Right
Article 19(1)(f)
Article 301
x: Article 300A protects against deprivation of property without authority of law and operates against executive action. Article 301 and the deleted Articles 31 and 19(1)(f) do not provide the applicable present remedy.
tq: Ask which constitutional provision governs the action of the authority actually dispossessing the person.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: Which one of the following statements regarding enforcement of Article 300A is correct?
o: It can be enforced only by filing a petition before the Election Commission
It cannot be enforced through any judicial proceeding
It can be enforced only through Article 32
It can be enforced through Article 226 or an ordinary civil suit, but not through Article 32 as a Fundamental Right
x: Since Article 300A does not confer a Fundamental Right, a claim may be pursued under Article 226 or through an ordinary suit, rather than as an Article 32 Fundamental Rights petition.
tq: Use the remedy-based distinction between Fundamental Rights and other constitutional rights.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s:
Which of the following statements regarding the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 is correct?
1. Social Impact Assessment is mandatory.
2. Consent of 70 per cent is required for public-private partnership projects.
3. Consent of 80 per cent is required for private projects.
4. Unused acquired land is to be returned after five years.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: The 2013 Act replaced the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and provides for mandatory Social Impact Assessment, 70 per cent consent for PPP projects, 80 per cent for private projects and return of unused land after five years.
tq: Separate the consent percentages and test all numerical conditions individually.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: Under the Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, the maximum compensation mentioned for rural and urban areas respectively is—
o: Twice the market value in both areas
Four times the market value in both areas
Four times the market value and twice the market value
Twice the market value and four times the market value
x: The compensation may be up to four times the market value in rural areas and twice the market value in urban areas.
tq: Read the comparison in the stated order: rural first and urban second.
sec: Right to property - Article 31 journey, deleting amendment, Article 300A

s: Article 30(1A), inserted by the 44th Amendment, deals primarily with—
o: Exemption of minority institutions from all State regulation
Compulsory acquisition of property of minority educational institutions
Appointment of teachers in minority institutions
Reservation of seats in minority institutions
x: Article 30(1A) concerns compulsory acquisition of the property of a minority educational institution. The amount fixed must not restrict or abrogate the right guaranteed by Article 30.
tq: Link the sub-clause number with its specific subject instead of the general right under Article 30(1).
sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

s:
Consider the following statements about Article 30:
1. The State shall not discriminate against minority institutions in granting aid.
2. The right to administer a minority institution is completely immune from State regulation.
3. The State may regulate standards of education without destroying the minority character of the institution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The right under Article 30 is not absolute; the State may regulate educational standards, but it cannot destroy the minority character of the institution.
tq: Reject the absolute statement while retaining the distinction between regulation of standards and destruction of minority character.
sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

s: The 25 per cent quota under the Right to Education Act does not apply to minority schools in view of the decision in—
o: St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
Pramati Educational and Cultural Trust v. Union of India
P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra
x: In Pramati, decided in 2014, the Supreme Court held that the RTE Act's 25 per cent quota does not apply to minority schools.
tq: Distinguish the case concerning RTE exemption from cases concerning autonomy, preference or reservation.
sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

s: According to the cited NCPCR figure, disadvantaged enrolment in minority schools was approximately—
o: 5.87 per cent
8.76 per cent
12.50 per cent
25 per cent
x: The cited NCPCR figure is 8.76 per cent disadvantaged enrolment in minority schools.
tq: Identify the precise percentage rather than confusing it with the RTE quota figure of 25 per cent.
sec: Article 30 - minority educational institutions, compensation clause

s: Article 29(1) protects the right of—
o: All persons, including non-citizens, to preserve any cultural practice
Only religious minorities to conserve their religion
Any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture to conserve the same
Only linguistic minorities to establish educational institutions
x: Article 29(1) grants any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture the right to conserve it. Its wording is wider than the term 'minorities'.
tq: Focus on the wider phrase 'any section of citizens' instead of narrowing it to minorities.
sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

s: Which one of the following grounds is NOT expressly included in Article 29(2) as a basis for denying admission to a State-maintained or State-aided educational institution?
o: Race
Place of birth
Religion
Language
x: Article 29(2) prohibits denial of admission on grounds only of religion, race, caste or language. Sex and place of birth are not included in this list.
tq: Find the omitted ground rather than selecting one of the four expressly listed grounds.
sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

s:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 29:
1. Article 29(1) is available to any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture.
2. Article 29(2) protects admission to State-maintained or State-aided institutions.
3. The protection under Article 29 is available to non-citizens also.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Article 29 is available only to citizens, so statement 3 is false.
tq: Test both the substantive protection and the class of persons entitled to it.
sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

s: A political promise to conserve the language of a particular section of citizens is, by itself, treated under the Representation of the People Act, 1951 as—
o: A violation of Article 30(2)
Not a corrupt practice
An electoral offence in every case
A corrupt practice
x: A political promise to conserve a section's language is not treated as a corrupt practice under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
tq: Distinguish a cultural or linguistic promise from a legally defined corrupt electoral practice.
sec: Article 29 - interests of minorities, language, script, culture, admission

s: Which one of the following correctly matches the right with its constitutional position?
o: Right to Vote — Article 326 and statutory provisions under the Representation of the People Acts
Right to Work — Article 21A
Right to Information — Article 41 only
Education for children aged 6–14 — Article 45 alone
x: Voting is based on adult suffrage under Article 326 and statutory provisions including Sections 62 of the RPA, 1951 and 19 of the RPA, 1950. The other options misstate the constitutional sources of work, information and education.
tq: Trace each right to its precise Article and statutory mechanism rather than relying on its general name.

s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Case)
A. In re Kerala Education Bill
B. St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi
C. T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka
D. P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra

List-II (Holding)
1. State is the unit for determining a linguistic or religious minority
2. Aided minority college may prefer its own community up to 50 per cent of seats
3. State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
4. State may regulate standards without destroying minority character

Select the correct answer.
x: In re Kerala Education Bill corresponds to regulation of standards; St. Stephen's permits preference up to 50 per cent; T.M.A. Pai identifies the State as the unit; and P.A. Inamdar rejects such State-imposed reservation in the stated institutions.
tq: Start from the distinctive case holdings and then verify the remaining pairs.

s: In St. Stephen's College v. University of Delhi, the Supreme Court held that an aided minority college may prefer candidates from its own community up to—
o: 33 per cent of the seats
25 per cent of the seats
75 per cent of the seats
50 per cent of the seats
x: The decision recognised that an aided minority college may prefer candidates from its own community up to 50 per cent of the seats.
tq: Distinguish the case-specific percentage from the separate 25 per cent RTE quota figure.

s: The decision in P.A. Inamdar v. State of Maharashtra is associated with which proposition?
o: The State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions
The RTE 25 per cent quota applies to all minority schools
The State may impose reservation on unaided minority professional institutions
Minority rights under Article 30 are entirely absolute
x: P.A. Inamdar held that the State cannot impose reservation on unaided minority or non-minority professional institutions in the manner stated.
tq: Identify the case by its specific reservation holding and reject absolute formulations.

s: For determining whether a group is a linguistic minority in a State, which one of the following is the appropriate unit of reference?
o: The concerned district only
The entire territory of India
The Union Territory having the largest population of that language
The concerned State
x: The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority. The test also considers numerical inferiority, non-dominant status and distinct identity.
tq: Use the constitutional unit of comparison rather than the size of the group at the national level.

s: Which of the following combination of criteria is relevant for determining a linguistic minority?
o: Numerical inferiority, non-dominant status in the State and distinct identity
Religious affiliation, urban residence and educational backwardness
Numerical superiority, political dominance and common occupation
District-level residence, income status and electoral representation
x: Determination involves numerical inferiority, non-dominant status in the State and a distinct linguistic identity.
tq: Identify the complete set of linked criteria instead of relying on numerical strength alone.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding linguistic minorities in India:
1. The Constitution expressly defines the expression “linguistic minority”.
2. The State is the unit for determining a linguistic minority.
3. Numerical inferiority and non-dominant status are relevant considerations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Constitution does not expressly define “linguistic minority”; therefore, statement 1 is false.
tq: Reject the statement carrying an incorrect constitutional definition while retaining the two substantive tests.

s: The National Commission for Minorities is best described as a:
o: Judicial body established under the Protection of Civil Rights Act
Statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
Constitutional body established under Article 350B
Non-statutory advisory body created by executive resolution
x: The National Commission for Minorities is a statutory body established under the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992.
tq: Distinguish a statutory commission from a constitutional office and an executive body.

s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six religious minorities notified for the purposes of the National Commission for Minorities?
o: Parsis
Jains
Linguistic minorities as a general category
Buddhists
x: The six notified religious minorities are Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains. “Linguistic minorities” is not one of the six notified religious categories.
tq: Find the category that does not belong to the notified religious-minority list.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Article)
 a. Article 347
 b. Article 350
 c. Article 350A
 d. Article 350B

List-II (Provision)
 i. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
 ii. Representation for grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
 iii. Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
 iv. Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic-minority children

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv
a–iv, b–i, c–ii, d–iii
a–i, b–iv, c–iii, d–ii
x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State; Article 350 concerns language for grievances; Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction; and Article 350B provides for the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
tq: Start with the sure Article–provision pair and eliminate codes that disturb the remaining relationships.

s: Under Article 347 of the Constitution, the President may recognise:
o: Any foreign language demanded by a linguistic minority
A language spoken by a substantial part of the population of a State
Only the language spoken by the majority of the State
Only the official language of the Union for use in a State
x: Article 347 empowers the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of the population of a State.
tq: Test the precise constitutional trigger and avoid extreme words such as “only”.

s: A person submits a representation for the redress of a grievance in a language used in the Union or in the State. Which constitutional provision is directly relevant?
o: Article 347
Article 350
Article 350A
Article 350B
x: Article 350 provides for representation for the redress of grievances in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State.
tq: Match the practical administrative situation with the exact Article dealing with grievances.

s: The constitutional provision relating to instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children belonging to linguistic minority groups is:
o: Article 347
Article 350A
Article 350B
Article 350
x: Article 350A deals with facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage for children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
tq: Discriminate between the closely numbered Articles 350, 350A and 350B by their functions.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Article 350B is correct?
o: It creates the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
It enables the President to recognise a language spoken by a substantial part of a State.
It permits grievances to be submitted only in the official language of the Union.
It guarantees mother-tongue instruction in all stages of education.
x: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, also known as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
tq: Separate the office-creating provision from the neighbouring language-related safeguards.

s: A publication prints the constitutional clause concerning mother-tongue instruction for linguistic-minority children as Article 360A. What is the correct constitutional Article?
o: Article 350A
Article 360A
Article 350B
Article 347A
x: The mother-tongue instruction clause is contained in Article 350A. Article 360A is a misprint in the cited publication.
tq: Prefer the exact constitutional provision over a look-alike Article number.

s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 31B — Laws concerning acquisition of estates and agrarian reform
Article 31A — Acts placed in the Ninth Schedule
Article 31C — Laws implementing Article 39(b) and Article 39(c)
Article 350A — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
x: Article 31C protects laws implementing Article 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19, subject to the constitutional and judicial limitations. Article 31A concerns estate acquisition and agrarian reform, Article 31B concerns Ninth Schedule laws, and Article 350B creates the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities.
tq: Check each Article against its precise subject and identify the only correctly matched pair.

s: Article 31C was inserted by the:
o: Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971
Forty-Second Amendment Act, 1976
Forty-Fourth Amendment Act, 1978
First Amendment Act, 1951
x: Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971 to protect laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19.
tq: Separate the amendment associated with Article 31C from the First Amendment associated with Articles 31A and 31B.

s: Which one of the following statements about the Ninth Schedule is correct?
o: It contains only laws implementing Article 39(b) and Article 39(c).
It contains fewer than 50 entries and enjoys complete immunity from judicial review.
It has grown to more than 280 entries, but inclusion does not confer blanket immunity from judicial review.
It has grown to more than 280 entries, and its contents have no constitutional relationship with Fundamental Rights.
x: The Ninth Schedule has grown to more than 280 entries, but inclusion does not provide blanket immunity from judicial review, particularly after the decisions in Waman Rao and I.R. Coelho.
tq: Reject the absolute claim of complete immunity and combine the numerical fact with the judicial limitation.

s: In Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981), the Supreme Court held that laws added to the Ninth Schedule after which date could be tested against the basic structure doctrine?
o: 18 June 1951
24 April 1973
26 January 1950
24 April 1981
x: Waman Rao treated laws added to the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 as open to challenge on the basis of the basic structure doctrine.
tq: Test the decisive cut-off date associated with the judicial review of Ninth Schedule entries.

s: Which one of the following best describes the effect of the decision in I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007)?
o: Only laws enacted before 1973 may be challenged under Article 31B.
Article 31B was declared entirely unconstitutional.
Ninth Schedule entries made after 1973 may be invalidated if they damage the essence of Articles 14, 19 or 21.
Every Ninth Schedule law is permanently immune from judicial review.
x: I.R. Coelho held that there is no blanket immunity for post-1973 Ninth Schedule entries; they can be invalidated if they damage the essence of Articles 14, 19 or 21.
tq: Identify the judicial qualification that defeats an absolute immunity statement.

s: The year 2026 marked how many years of the First Amendment to the Constitution?
o: 50 years
65 years
75 years
85 years
x: The First Amendment was enacted in 1951, making 2026 its 75th anniversary. It received the assent of President Rajendra Prasad.
tq: Calculate the anniversary from the amendment year and distinguish it from later constitutional amendments.

s:
Which of the following were associated with the First Amendment Act, 1951?
1. Insertion of Article 15(4)
2. Insertion of Articles 31A and 31B
3. Addition of public order, friendly relations with foreign States and incitement as grounds under Article 19(2)
4. Insertion of Article 31C
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1, 2 and 3 only
1 and 4 only
2, 3 and 4 only
x: The First Amendment added Article 15(4), Articles 31A and 31B, and the stated grounds under Article 19(2). Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment Act, 1971.
tq: Separate provisions belonging to the First Amendment from the closely related provision inserted by the Twenty-Fifth Amendment.

s: Which recent development was reported as creating concern regarding the Kannada linguistic minority in Kasaragod?
o: A central notification replacing all State languages with Hindi
A constitutional amendment abolishing Article 350A
A Malayalam language Bill in Kerala receiving assent in March 2026
A judicial decision removing the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
x: The Kerala Malayalam Bhasha Bill received assent in March 2026 and was contested on the ground that it could harm the Kannada linguistic minority in Kasaragod.
tq: Connect the current-affairs development with the precise linguistic-minority issue involved.

s: Which one of the following concerns has been raised in debates relating to minority educational institutions?
o: The abolition of the National Commission for Minorities Act, 1992
A constitutional prohibition on minority-run schools receiving any public assistance
A complete prohibition on mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Misuse of minority status to avoid obligations under the Right to Education framework
x: A criticism in the debate is that minority status may sometimes be misused to escape obligations under the Right to Education framework.
tq: Identify the stated criticism without converting it into an absolute constitutional prohibition.

s: The criticism that amendments to the Foreign Contribution Regulation Act may threaten minority-run civil society organisations relates to:
o: The appointment of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities
FCRA amendments and their effect on minority-run civil society
Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule
Article 347 and recognition of State languages
x: The stated concern is that FCRA amendments may pose a threat to minority-run civil society organisations.
tq: Match the policy measure with the specific civil-society concern rather than a constitutional language provision.

s: In GGR Housing v. State, the Andhra Pradesh High Court emphasised:
o: Strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A
The abolition of Article 300A as a legal right
The conversion of the right to property into a Fundamental Right
The exclusion of land acquisition from judicial review
x: The Andhra Pradesh High Court insisted on strict statutory due process in land acquisition under Article 300A. Article 300A protects the right to property as a legal constitutional right.
tq: Apply the case principle to the constitutional protection governing deprivation of property.

s: The Andhra Pradesh minority cell fast-tracked direct benefit transfer of post-matric scholarships subject to an income ceiling of:
o: Rs 5 lakh
Rs 1 lakh
Rs 2 lakh
Rs 2.5 lakh
x: The reported post-matric scholarship initiative applied an income ceiling of Rs 2.5 lakh and used direct benefit transfer.
tq: Recall the precise eligibility ceiling and distinguish it from nearby round-number distractors.

s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 31C — Protection of laws relating to acquisition of estates from Articles 14 and 19
Article 350B — Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage
Article 347 — Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial part of a State
x: Article 31C protects laws implementing Article 39(b) and (c) from challenge under Articles 14 and 19. Protection for laws relating to acquisition of estates and agrarian reform is associated with Article 31A.
tq: Find the swapped subject between the neighbouring provisions of Articles 31A and 31C.
